questions.question: In March 2025, the Union Home Minister inaugurated the Lachit Barphukan Police Academy in Assam to honour his legacy. Who was Lachit Barphukan?

options.text: A military commander of the Mughals
A commander of the Ahom kingdom

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**A commander of the Ahom kingdom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lachit Barphukan** was a legendary military commander of the **Ahom kingdom**, which ruled over present-day Assam.
 
• He is best known for his role in the **Battle of Saraighat** (1671), where he led the Ahom forces to victory against the invading **Mughal army.**
 
• The Battle of Saraighat is considered a significant event in Indian history as it prevented the Mughal expansion into the northeastern region of India.
 
• Lachit Barphukan demonstrated exceptional leadership, military strategy, and patriotism during the battle.
 
• He is celebrated for his famous quote, "**My duty to my king and my country comes before my family**," which he proved by punishing his own uncle for negligence during the war.
 
• His legacy symbolizes **courage, selflessness, and loyalty** to the nation, making him an enduring figure of Assamese pride.
 
• The Lachit Barphukan Police Academy in Assam has been named in his honor to inspire future generations with his values and contributions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **A military commander of the Mughals**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because Lachit Barphukan was not associated with the Mughal Empire but fought against it in the Battle of Saraighat.
 
• The Mughal Empire, under Emperor Aurangzeb, sought to expand its territory into Assam during Lachit Barphukan's time.
 
 
 
• **A poet from Assam**__
 __
 
• Lachit Barphukan was not a poet but a military commander. However, Assam has a rich tradition of poetry and literature, including works by renowned poets like **Jyoti Prasad Agarwala** and **Hem Barua**.
 
 
 
• **A British-era police officer**__
 
 
• This option is incorrect as Lachit Barphukan lived in the 17th century, long before the British colonial rule in India.
 
• British-era police officers were introduced during the colonial administration, mainly for maintaining law and order under British governance.

questions.question: Who is the Chairperson of Lokpal as of April 2025 in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice Ajay Manik Rao Khanwilkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Justice Ajay Manik Rao Khanwilkar was appointed as the Chairperson of Lokpal in India as of April 2025.
 
• Lokpal is an anti-corruption authority established under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.
 
• The Chairperson of Lokpal is selected by a committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, and an eminent jurist nominated by the President.
 
• Justice Khanwilkar has previously served as a judge in the Supreme Court of India and has been known for his contributions to judicial reforms.
 
• The Lokpal consists of a Chairperson and members, including judicial and non-judicial members, who work to investigate cases of corruption against public servants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013:** This act provides for the establishment of Lokpal at the central level and Lokayuktas at the state level to address corruption in governance.
 
• **Composition of Lokpal:** Lokpal includes a Chairperson and up to eight members, with at least 50% of them being judicial members and 50% belonging to SC/ST/OBC/minorities or women.
 
• **Jurisdiction:** Lokpal has jurisdiction over the Prime Minister (with certain safeguards), Ministers, Members of Parliament, and Group A, B, C, and D government officials.
 
• **Investigation Process:** The Lokpal can order a preliminary inquiry through its Inquiry Wing or direct a probe through the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).
 
• **Significance:** Lokpal is a vital institution in ensuring accountability and transparency in governance, strengthening the fight against corruption in India.

questions.question: Kumudini Rajnikant Lakhia was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan in 2025 for her contribution in which field?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kumudini Rajnikant Lakhia is a renowned Indian classical dancer and choreographer specializing in **Kathak dance**.
 
• She has played a pivotal role in **modernizing and globalizing Kathak** while preserving its traditional essence.
 
• Her work spans several decades, and she is recognized for revolutionizing Kathak through innovative choreography and **group presentations**.
 
• She founded the **Kadamb Center for Dance and Music** in Ahmedabad to nurture and promote the art of Kathak.
 
• The Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian award, was conferred upon her in 2025 for her **exceptional contributions to the field of Arts**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak Dance:** Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures.
 
• **Padma Vibhushan:** Instituted in 1954, the Padma Vibhushan is India's second-highest civilian award, given for exceptional service in various fields.
 
• **Kadamb Center for Dance and Music:** Founded by Kumudini Lakhia, this institution is a hub for Kathak training, research, and innovation.
 
• **Innovative Choreography:** Kumudini Lakhia is celebrated for introducing group choreography to Kathak, a departure from its traditional solo performances.
 
• **Contributions to Arts:** Kumudini Lakhia's work has significantly influenced contemporary dance and inspired countless dancers globally.

questions.question: In January 2025, National Tourism Day was celebrated with which of the following themes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tourism for Inclusive Growth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• National Tourism Day in India is celebrated annually on **25th January** to raise awareness about the significance of tourism for the country's economy and culture.
 
• The theme for National Tourism Day 2025 was **Tourism for Inclusive Growth**, which emphasizes creating opportunities for all, particularly marginalized communities.
 
• This theme aligns with the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, focusing on reducing inequalities and fostering social and economic development through tourism.
 
• Inclusive tourism practices ensure that local communities benefit from the economic and cultural opportunities provided by tourism, promoting equitable growth.
 
• The celebration of National Tourism Day 2025 included campaigns, workshops, and events aimed at highlighting the importance of sustainable and inclusive tourism practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tourism in India:**

 
 
• India is one of the most visited countries globally, known for its cultural heritage, diverse geography, and historical landmarks.
 
• The tourism sector contributes significantly to India's GDP and employment, accounting for approximately **9.2% of GDP** and supporting millions of jobs.
 
 
 
• **Inclusive Growth:**
 
 
• It refers to economic growth that is distributed fairly across society and creates opportunities for all.
 
• In tourism, this involves supporting local communities, creating equitable job opportunities, and promoting cultural exchange.
 
 
 
• **United Nations World Tourism Organization (UNWTO):**
 
 
• The UNWTO promotes sustainable and inclusive tourism globally.
 
• It works to ensure that tourism contributes to poverty reduction, environmental protection, and cultural preservation.
 
 
 
• **National Tourism Policy 2022 (India):**
 
 
• This policy aims to position India as a global leader in sustainable tourism by promoting responsible practices.
 
• It emphasizes eco-tourism, cultural tourism, and adventure tourism while integrating local communities into the tourism value chain.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Exercise Tiger Triumph – 25, which was conducted in April 2025.

 
• It was a bilateral Tri-Service Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) exercise between India and the United Kingdom.
 
• The Harbour Phase of the exercise was scheduled at Visakhapatnam, while the Sea Phase and HADR operations were conducted off Kakinada.
 
• Indian participation included INS Vikrant along with other Army and Air Force contingents.
 
• The exercise aimed to develop interoperability and formulate SOPs for a Combined Coordination Centre during joint operations.

Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 2 and 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Exercise Tiger Triumph – 25** is a bilateral Tri-Service Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) exercise conducted between India and the United States, not the United Kingdom.
 
• The Harbour Phase of the exercise was scheduled at **Visakhapatnam**, and the Sea Phase and HADR operations were conducted off **Kakinada**.
 
• The exercise aimed at enhancing **interoperability** between the forces of participating nations and formulating **Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)** for a Combined Coordination Centre during joint operations.
 
• Indian participation included major assets such as the **INS Vikrant**, along with other contingents from the Army and the Air Force.
 
• Statement 2 and 4 are correct, while statement 1 is incorrect as the exercise was not with the United Kingdom, and statement 3 is partially correct but not entirely specific to this exercise.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exercise Tiger Triumph**: A unique initiative that involves the **Indian Armed Forces** and the **United States Armed Forces** working together to improve disaster response capabilities.
 
• **INS Vikrant**: India’s first indigenously built aircraft carrier, commissioned in 2022. It plays a pivotal role in strengthening India's maritime capabilities.
 
• **Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) Operations**: These are operations conducted by military forces to provide relief during disasters like earthquakes, tsunamis, and cyclones, ensuring rapid and effective aid to affected areas.
 
• **Visakhapatnam and Kakinada**: Important coastal cities in Andhra Pradesh, India. Visakhapatnam serves as a significant naval base, while Kakinada is known for its strategic port activities.
 
• **Interoperability**: The ability of military forces from different nations to operate effectively together, involving the integration of procedures, equipment, and communication systems.

questions.question: According to INEP Emissions Gap Report 2024, what annual reduction in emissions is required until 2035 to limit global warming to 1.5°C?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.075**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2024 highlights that an annual reduction of **0.075 (7.5%) in global greenhouse gas emissions** is necessary until 2035 to limit global warming to 1.5°C.
 
• The report emphasizes that this rate of reduction aligns with the goals of the **Paris Agreement**, which aims to keep global temperature rise well below 2°C and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C.
 
• Current policies and pledges fall significantly short, requiring urgent action to bridge the emissions gap and achieve the 1.5°C target.
 
• Key sectors contributing to emissions include energy, industry, transportation, and agriculture, all of which need rapid decarbonization.
 
• Increased investments in renewable energy, energy efficiency, and carbon capture and storage (CCS) technologies are vital to achieve these reductions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Emissions Gap:** The difference between the current trajectory of greenhouse gas emissions and the levels needed to meet the Paris Agreement targets.
 
• **Paris Agreement:** An international treaty adopted in 2015 to combat climate change and strengthen global responses by limiting global warming to well below 2°C, preferably 1.5°C, above pre-industrial levels.
 
• **Greenhouse Gases (GHGs):** Gases like carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), and nitrous oxide (N2O) that trap heat in the atmosphere and contribute to global warming.
 
• **Carbon Neutrality:** Achieving a balance between emitted carbon dioxide and its removal from the atmosphere, often referred to as "net zero" emissions.
 
• **Renewable Energy:** Sources like solar, wind, and hydropower that produce energy without depleting natural resources or causing significant environmental harm.

questions.question: Between 2013-14 and 2022-23, how many Indians escaped multidimensional poverty, according to NITI Aayog?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**24.82 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to a report by NITI Aayog, **24.82 crore Indians escaped multidimensional poverty** between 2013-14 and 2022-23.
 
• This was revealed in the **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) Report** released in 2023.
 
• The reduction in multidimensional poverty was driven by improvements in areas such as **health, education, and living standards.**
 
• States like **Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, and Rajasthan** witnessed the largest reductions in poverty levels.
 
• The MPI measures poverty across three dimensions: **health, education, and standard of living**, using 12 indicators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**

 
 
• It is a globally recognized measure developed by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).
 
• MPI assesses poverty beyond income, focusing on **health, education, and living standards.**
 
• Indicators include nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, sanitation, drinking water, and housing quality.
 
 
 
• **Role of Government Schemes:**
 
 
• Initiatives such as **Ayushman Bharat, PM Awas Yojana, Swachh Bharat Mission, and Skill India** contributed significantly to poverty reduction.
 
• These schemes focused on improving access to healthcare, education, sanitation, and financial inclusion.
 
 
 
• **State-wise Performance:**
 
 
• States like **Kerala and Tamil Nadu** consistently rank high in poverty reduction due to better governance and social infrastructure.
 
• **Bihar** saw a significant drop in multidimensional poverty, although it still has a higher proportion of poor compared to other states.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective:**
 
 
• India’s success in reducing multidimensional poverty is seen as a major contributor to global poverty alleviation efforts.
 
• The country’s efforts align with the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 1)** of eradicating poverty in all its forms.

questions.question: As per the Global Gender Gap Report, 2024, what percentage of the gender gap has India closed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.641**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the **Global Gender Gap Report 2024**, India has closed **64.1% of its overall gender gap**.
 
• This marks a significant improvement in India's ranking and performance in addressing gender-based inequalities.
 
• The Global Gender Gap Index is published by the **World Economic Forum (WEF)** and evaluates gender parity across four key dimensions: Economic Participation, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, and Political Empowerment.
 
• India ranks **within the top 20% of countries globally** in terms of political empowerment, largely due to the high representation of women in political leadership.
 
• Despite progress, challenges remain in areas such as **labour force participation and economic opportunities** for women.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Gender Gap Index:**

 
 
• Introduced by the World Economic Forum (WEF) in 2006 to track progress on gender parity globally.
 
• Ranks countries based on their performance across four dimensions: Economic Participation, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, and Political Empowerment.
 
• The index uses a scale from 0 (imparity) to 1 (parity).
 
 
 
• **India's Performance:**
 
 
• In 2024, India has shown improvement in areas like **political empowerment**, driven by an increased number of women in leadership roles.
 
• However, challenges persist in the **economic participation** of women due to factors like wage gaps and employment opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Global Insights:**
 
 
• Iceland continues to top the Global Gender Gap Index, maintaining its position as the most gender-equal country.
 
• On average, the world has closed 69% of the gender gap, with varying progress across regions.
 
 
 
• **Key Challenges:**
 
 
• Barriers such as limited access to education, healthcare, and financial resources for women continue to hinder progress in many nations.
 
• Efforts to close the gender gap require targeted policy interventions and societal change.

questions.question: Which international entity has partnered with India to launch joint research initiatives aimed at tackling marine plastic litter and developing waste-to-hydrogen technologies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**European Union (EU)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **European Union (EU)** has partnered with India to jointly address the issue of marine plastic litter and advance waste-to-hydrogen technologies.
 
• This collaboration is part of a larger initiative to tackle environmental challenges and promote sustainable technologies globally.
 
• India and the EU are focusing on **joint research and innovation** in the field of environmental sustainability.
 
• The partnership aligns with the EU's **European Green Deal** and India's **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan** objectives to combat pollution and promote clean energy solutions.
 
• Collaborative efforts include developing advanced technologies for **plastic waste management** and harnessing hydrogen as a clean energy resource.

• **European Green Deal:** A set of policy initiatives by the EU aimed at making Europe climate-neutral by 2050.

questions.question: Where did Max Verstappen clinch his fourth Formula 1 World Championship?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Las Vegas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Max Verstappen sealed his **fourth consecutive** World Drivers’ Championship at the **2024 Las Vegas Grand Prix** on November 24, 2024.
 
• A **P5 finish** in Las Vegas gave him an **unassailable 63-point lead** over Lando Norris with two races remaining.
 
• The Las Vegas race was **won by George Russell** (Lewis Hamilton P2); Verstappen’s P5 was enough to clinch the title.
 
• It was the **third time** an F1 title was decided in Las Vegas, after **1981 (Piquet)** and **1982 (Rosberg)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Miami** is a separate U.S. race (first held in **2022**) at the Miami International Autodrome in Miami Gardens—*not* where the title was clinched.
 
• **Austin** hosts the United States Grand Prix at **Circuit of The Americas** (since 2012), a different venue and event.
 
• **Indianapolis** last hosted the U.S. GP in **2007**; F1 has not raced there since, ruling it out as the clinching venue.

questions.question: Which Indian state's/Union Territory's government has announced its Electric Vehicle (EV) Policy 2.0 to reduce air pollution in the region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Delhi Government announced its **Electric Vehicle (EV) Policy 2.0** in August 2023 to strengthen its efforts to combat air pollution and promote clean mobility.
 
• The policy aims to make Delhi a leading state/UT in EV adoption by achieving a target of **80% electrification in new vehicle registrations** by 2026.
 
• **Incentives** such as subsidies for EV buyers, tax exemptions, and reduced registration fees are part of the policy framework to boost EV adoption.
 
• Under EV Policy 2.0, Delhi plans to expand charging infrastructure by setting up **charging stations and battery swapping facilities** across the city.
 
• The initiative is aligned with India's broader goals of achieving sustainable and green transportation solutions and reducing dependence on fossil fuels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electric Vehicle (EV) Terminology:**

 
 
• **Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs):** Fully electric vehicles powered by rechargeable battery packs with zero emissions.
 
• **Hybrid Electric Vehicles (HEVs):** Vehicles combining a conventional internal combustion engine with an electric propulsion system.
 
• **Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicles (PHEVs):** Hybrid vehicles with rechargeable batteries that can be charged externally.
 
 
 
• **Impact of EV Adoption:**
 
 
• Reduces greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution, contributing to better public health and environmental sustainability.
 
• Decreases dependency on fossil fuels, enhancing energy security in the region.
 
 
 
• **Charging Infrastructure:**
 
 
• Delhi’s EV Policy 2.0 emphasizes the deployment of charging stations at strategic locations, including public places and residential complexes.
 
• Battery swapping stations aim to improve convenience for EV users, facilitating quick changes of depleted batteries.
 
 
 
• **Government Role in EV Promotion:**
 
 
• Subsidies and tax exemptions play a key role in reducing the initial cost of EVs.
 
• Awareness campaigns and partnerships with private entities are critical to accelerating EV adoption.

questions.question: Who among the following was appointed as the Chairman of the Airports Authority of India (AAI), in October 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vipin Kumar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vipin Kumar was appointed as the Chairman of the Airports Authority of India (AAI) in **October 2024**.
 
• The Airports Authority of India is a **statutory body under the Ministry of Civil Aviation**, responsible for creating, upgrading, maintaining, and managing civil aviation infrastructure in India.
 
• Vipin Kumar's appointment comes with the mandate to oversee critical modernization projects and ensure the growth and sustainability of India's aviation sector.
 
• He has extensive experience in aviation management and has previously held significant roles within the aviation sector.
 
• His leadership is expected to enhance India's airport infrastructure, focusing on passenger experience and operational efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Airports Authority of India (AAI):**

 
 
• Established in 1995, the AAI manages 137 airports in India, including 24 international airports, 10 customs airports, and 103 domestic airports.
 
• AAI is responsible for providing **Air Traffic Management (ATM)** services over Indian airspace and adjoining oceanic areas.

questions.question: In October 2024, the Indian government notified rules under the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023. What was a key objective of this legislation?

options.text: To convert minor offenses under various laws from criminal to civil penalties
To legalise digital signatures for land registration documents
To expand the RTI Act to cover private educational institutions
To establish a unified grievance redressal portal for all central ministries

questions.solution:

• The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023, aims to promote ease of business by reducing compliance burdens.
 
• It seeks to convert minor offenses under 42 legislations from criminal offenses to civil penalties, fostering a business-friendly environment.
 
• The law aims to decriminalize petty offenses across various domains, including trade, commerce, and industry.
 
• By reducing criminal penalties for minor infractions, the Act encourages entrepreneurship and reduces fear of legal repercussions for small errors.
 
• The Act aligns with the government’s broader agenda of improving India's ranking in the Ease of Doing Business index.

• Decriminalization involves removing criminal penalties for certain acts, replacing them with civil penalties or administrative actions.
 
• This approach is used to reduce the burden on the judiciary and improve compliance without harsh legal consequences.
 
 
 
• **Ease of Doing Business:**
 
 
• India has been working to improve its Ease of Doing Business ranking globally, focusing on streamlining regulations and reducing barriers for businesses.
 
• Measures like decriminalization of minor offenses are integral to achieving this goal.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Business Ecosystem:**
 
 
• By converting criminal penalties to civil penalties, businesses can avoid lengthy legal disputes and focus on growth.
 
• This reform benefits startups and small enterprises, encouraging innovation and entrepreneurship.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Scope:**
 
 
• The Jan Vishwas Act amends 42 laws, including regulations related to environment, labor, and consumer protection.
 
• It ensures uniformity in penalties and simplifies compliance frameworks across sectors.

• Fentanyl is a synthetic opioid that is 50-100 times more potent than morphine.
 
• It is used medically for pain relief but is often illegally manufactured and distributed as a recreational drug.
 
• Because of its high potency, even a small amount can lead to overdose and death.
 
 
 
• **Opioid Epidemic:**
 
 
• The opioid epidemic refers to the widespread misuse of opioids, including prescription pain relievers, heroin, and synthetic opioids like fentanyl.
 
• It has led to significant increases in addiction, overdose deaths, and societal costs globally, especially in the U.S.

• Cross-border drug trafficking is a major issue contributing to the global drug crisis, including fentanyl distribution.
 
• It often involves organized crime syndicates and poses challenges for international law enforcement agencies.

questions.question: What was India’s external debt to GDP ratio at the end of September 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.194**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's external debt to GDP ratio at the end of September 2024 was **19.4% (0.194)**, indicating a moderate level of external debt relative to its GDP.
 
• This ratio is a critical indicator of a country’s ability to manage and repay its external debt obligations efficiently.
 
• A lower external debt-to-GDP ratio is generally considered favorable as it reflects a lower debt burden in comparison to the country’s economic output.
 
• India has consistently maintained a sustainable external debt level, supported by its strong foreign exchange reserves.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) periodically monitors and publishes data on the country's external debt to ensure transparency and economic stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **External Debt:**

 
 
• External debt refers to the total borrowing by a country from foreign lenders, including governments, financial institutions, and private entities.
 
• It typically includes loans, bonds, and other financial instruments owed to non-residents.
 
 
 
• **External Debt to GDP Ratio:**
 
 
• This ratio is calculated by dividing a country’s total external debt by its Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
 
• A lower ratio indicates that the country’s economic output is sufficient to cover its debt obligations, reducing the risk of default.
 
 
 
• **India’s External Debt Composition:**
 
 
• India’s external debt is categorized into short-term and long-term debt, with long-term debt constituting a significant share.
 
• Major components include commercial borrowings, NRI deposits, and multilateral loans.
 
 
 
• **Role of Foreign Exchange Reserves:**
 
 
• India’s foreign exchange reserves act as a buffer to manage external debt obligations and ensure economic stability.
 
• As of recent years, India has maintained substantial reserves to meet its debt servicing requirements comfortably.
